source_name: TED eSenders list (SK: zoznam elektronických odosielateľov)
why_relevant: Identifies which Slovak systems/organisations transmit notices to TED (ÚVO eForms IS and any commercial eSenders). Reveals the upstream national systems whose data can be tapped directly and explains publication lags/duplication between ÚVO Vestník and TED.

source_name: TED release calendar (kalendár zverejnenia Úradného vestníka série S)
why_relevant: Publication schedule of the OJ S series; needed to time collection jobs and to interpret gaps in Slovak notice flow as calendar effects rather than market signals.

source_name: SIMAP — European public procurement information (SK version)
why_relevant: Explains thresholds, CPV nomenclature and the legal basis that determines which Slovak banking/payment contracts must appear at EU level — the rulebook for interpreting coverage and for setting CPV filters.

source_name: EUR-Lex — Official Journal direct access (Úradný vestník EÚ, SK)
why_relevant: Authoritative archive of the Official Journal in Slovak; useful for legal-status confirmation of procurement rules and for OJ items (state aid, banking-sector decisions) that contextualise Slovak banking procurement but sit outside the S-series.

source_name: EU Funding & Tenders Portal (SEDIA) — procurement/opportunities
why_relevant: Single entry point for centrally managed EU tenders and grants. Captures EU-institution contracts and programme calls (Digital Europe, Horizon, TSI) where Slovak banks, fintechs or the NBS ecosystem appear as bidders/beneficiaries — spend that never reaches ÚVO.

source_name: EU F&T Portal eProcurement wiki (technical/API documentation)
why_relevant: Documents the portal's data model and access routes, which is how a collector can move from manual browsing to scheduled retrieval of EU-institution tender records relevant to Slovak financial-sector suppliers.

source_name: EBRD Client e-Procurement Portal (ECEPP) — procurement notices
why_relevant: Since the EBRD consolidated publication, ECEPP is the only channel for procurement, prequalification and award notices under EBRD-financed projects. Slovak clients (e.g. SEPS-type public-sector borrowers, financial-institution TC assignments) publish here, and these contracts never appear in the ÚVO bulletin.

source_name: EBRD procurement notices (ebrd.com landing/filtered listing)
why_relevant: Institutional entry point explaining notice types and routing to ECEPP; also carries the guidance note defining what must be published, which sets expectations for coverage of Slovak operations.

source_name: EBRD corporate procurement & consultancy services
why_relevant: EBRD's own-account purchasing of banking/payment-related advisory and IT services; occasionally scopes assignments covering Slovakia or CEE financial-infrastructure diagnostics, signalling upcoming projects before any national tender exists.

source_name: EIB project pages for Slovakia (eib.org/projects)
why_relevant: EIB project records name Slovak financial-sector intermediaries and beneficiaries (e.g. Eximbanka SR SME/mid-cap lines, EU 2021-2027 co-financing) and state procurement arrangements. These identify institutions likely to run banking/IT procurements and indicate the funding envelope behind them.

source_name: EIB press releases — Slovakia country stream
why_relevant: Earliest public signal of new EIB Group operations in Slovakia, including intermediated lending through Slovak banks — a leading indicator of downstream procurement and of which banks are scaling programmes.

source_name: Ministry of Finance SR — International financial institutions / EIB page (MF SR)
why_relevant: Slovak-state view of its IFI relationships (EIB, EBRD, CEB, World Bank Group), naming the domestic counterparties and programmes through which IFI-financed procurement is channelled — the bridge between the EU/IFI layer and Slovak actors.

source_name: World Bank Group procurement notices (Finances One / Data Catalog)
why_relevant: Structured dataset of WBG-financed procurement notices. Slovakia is not a borrowing country, so volume is expected to be near-zero, but WBG Reimbursable Advisory Services in Slovakia can generate consultancy procurement touching public financial management/payments.

source_name: Opentender.eu — Slovakia country portal (DIGIWHIST)
why_relevant: Research-grade re-publication of TED plus the Slovak national procurement archive, with harmonised variables and corruption/competition-risk indicators. Useful as a cross-check on TED coverage and for supplier-level aggregation of Slovak banking/IT contracts.

source_name: Publications Office public-procurement procurement-details pages (op.europa.eu)
why_relevant: Publications Office front end presenting individual procurement records (including banking-services CPV 66110000 examples) with a stable UUID-based URL scheme; a secondary rendering of TED content useful for human verification and reusers' workshop material.

source_name: OP-TED eForms-SDK GitHub repository
why_relevant: Machine-readable codelists, schemas and issue tracker for the eForms standard — the practical reference when building a TED collector and when diagnosing why some Slovak fields are missing or coded unexpectedly.

source_name: ÚVO Vestník verejného obstarávania (national bulletin — cross-layer anchor)
why_relevant: Belongs to the national layer but is the required cross-reference for this cell: it carries below-threshold Slovak banking/payment contracts that never reach TED, and since Aug 2024 must publish results for all below-threshold contracts. Needed to measure TED's coverage shortfall for SK.

source_name: ÚVO – Dohľad (supervision hub: námietky, kontrola, správne delikty, Rada úradu)
why_relevant: Master entry point of the Slovak procurement review body (Úrad pre verejné obstarávanie) linking every remedy/oversight register: objections, review of contracting authority's acts, administrative offences (fines), inspections and the Council's appeal decisions. Everything in this coverage cell hangs off these subsections.

source_name: ÚVO – Prehľad rozhodnutí o námietkach (všeobecná agenda)
why_relevant: Decision-by-decision listing of objection (námietky) rulings. For banking/payments tenders (bankové služby, platobné karty, akceptácia platieb, POS terminály) these decisions disclose bid values, evaluation criteria, disqualified bidders and grounds for cancellation that the award notice never shows.

source_name: ÚVO – Prehľad rozhodnutí o námietkach (strategická agenda)
why_relevant: Separate track for strategic/large-value procurements (typically EU-funded or nationally significant). Large bank-service, cash-handling or payment-infrastructure contracts for ministries and state agencies are more likely to land here.

source_name: ÚVO – Zbierky rozhodnutí (curated decision collections / good-practice digests)
why_relevant: ÚVO's own thematic digests of decisions issued in objection proceedings — compact way to learn recurring failure patterns (e.g. conditions of participation, references, pricing) that shape how banking/payment tenders are written and contested in SK.

source_name: ÚVO – Správne delikty (administrative offences / fines register)
why_relevant: Sanction decisions naming contracting authorities fined for procurement breaches. Retrospectively exposes contracts awarded without proper competition — including direct awards of bank/payment services — with contract values and legal reasoning.

source_name: ÚVO – Kontrola (ex-ante / ex-post inspection decisions)
why_relevant: Inspection outcomes, including ex-ante assessment of high-value procurements. Ex-ante files can reveal a banking/payments tender's design before award, an early-warning channel.

source_name: Rada ÚVO – Prehľad rozhodnutí (appeal body decisions)
why_relevant: Second-instance appeal decisions against ÚVO rulings; the fullest legal record of a contested tender. Note a legislative change: the Council was made transitional and handles appeals against decisions issued up to 31 Dec 2022, so post-2022 second-instance review may sit elsewhere (chairman of the Office / courts) — the historical archive remains highly valuable.
